assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, incretin action, insulin-dependent glucose lowering and satiety) translated into incretin therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care. The conceptual step from hormone biology to durable, long-acting drugs and large outcome benefits is exceptionally clear and of broad lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and GLP-2, translational work), Holst (gut hormone physiology and GLP-1 secretion) and Knudsen (design of long-acting liraglutide/semaglutide) cover discovery, physiology and therapy. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is credited on the list, and the allocation among Mojsov, Habener and others is contested and cannot be resolved from the supplied text; the three-person limit forces an exclusion.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large cardiovascular, renal and weight outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the early identification of active GLP-1(7-36) amide is disputed and outside the supplied names for some contributors.
Industry-affiliated laureate raises a question of whether the committee wishes to recognize drug design alongside physiology.
Long-term safety and population-level effects are still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new class of living drug. The concept, engineering of costimulatory signaling and clinical proof are original and consequential.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB, first clinical successes), Sadelain (CD28-based second-generation CARs and preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials) form a plausible trio. Eshhar and others who contributed early CAR concepts are not in the supplied names, which is an unresolved allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, long-term remissions documented beyond a decade in some patients, and growing use in autoimmunity. Clearly mature, though extension to solid tumors remains limited.
uncertainties: Early CAR concept credit (not among the supplied names) is relevant to a fair prize configuration.
Toxicities, manufacturing cost and limited efficacy in solid tumors.
Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive cell therapy broadly, which may be a distinct discovery from CAR engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response as an intracellular ER-to-nucleus signaling pathway (Ire1, Hac1 splicing, XBP1) revealed how cells monitor and adjust protein-folding capacity. It is a fundamental, original mechanism with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer, and it connects to RNA processing in an unconventional cytoplasmic splicing event.
assessment.attribution: Walter (Ire1 as the transmembrane sensor/nuclease, Hac1 mRNA splicing) and Mori (UPR signaling and HAC1/XBP1 regulation) are the two decisive contributors named; the pairing is clean and concentrated.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is thoroughly confirmed over thirty years in yeast and mammals and has become textbook. The translational payoff is still emerging, but the basic science is fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether Walter's work on the ISR/ISRIB and other contributors (e.g., Ron, Kaufman, Schekman-linked groundwork) would be considered for recognition is unclear.
Clinical translation is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial channelrhodopsins were turned into tools for millisecond-precision, cell-type-specific control of neural activity, transforming causal neuroscience and enabling circuit-level studies of behavior and disease models. The invention opened a new experimental paradigm used across physiology.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization as light-gated channels, with Bamberg) and Deisseroth (neuronal implementation and broad application) are a plausible trio. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck are also strong claimants, so any three-person configuration leaves out a person with a substantial claim; priority among Boyden, Deisseroth and others in neuronal expression is contested.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for more than a decade; clinical translation (retinal vision restoration) has begun but remains early. As a tool and concept it is mature.
uncertainties: Contentious allocation of credit among six listed names, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck excluded by the size limit.
Direct therapeutic impact is still limited, and the prize category requires physiological or medical significance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed by cGAS, which synthesizes the second messenger 2'3'-cGAMP that activates STING and interferon responses. It explains innate immune responses to viruses, self-DNA in autoimmunity and tumor immunity, and is a clear and original mechanistic discovery with wide impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber discovered STING. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are credited but are lesser or trainee contributions. The pairing of Chen and Barber is the natural core; other early or parallel contributors (e.g., Vance, Tegtmeyer-linked cyclic dinucleotide work) are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across labs, but therapeutic exploitation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet produced a clear approved drug; timing could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Relative contributions of Barber versus others in the STING identification and cyclic dinucleotide biology are not resolvable from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-lived, self-organizing organoids from single Lgr5+ adult stem cells provided a new in vitro system for tissue biology, disease modelling, host-pathogen studies and personalized medicine. It follows the stem-cell identification of Lgr5 and builds a broadly adopted experimental platform.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and intestinal organoid work and Sato was first author on the key organoid papers. Contributions of Sasai (pluripotent-derived organoids) and Lancaster, Knoblich and others are outside this candidate's names, so the scope is limited to adult stem-cell organoids.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted and independently reproduced; clinical impact (drug screening, CF patient-derived organoids) is real but still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with embryonic or pluripotent-derived organoid fields complicates a clean discovery definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma and its use for noninvasive prenatal testing created a clinically deployed screening tool and a paradigm for liquid biopsy. The discovery is clear, original and has changed practice worldwide with a low-risk alternative to invasive sampling.
assessment.attribution: Lo's 1997 observation and subsequent technical developments are a single-person, well-defined contribution. Companies and groups developing sequencing-based aneuploidy detection contributed to implementation, but the founding discovery is clearly attributed.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation and global clinical use; extensions to cancer detection are ongoing.
uncertainties: Whether a diagnostic/technology advance fits as a physiology or medicine discovery of the highest scientific rank.
Contributions of massively parallel sequencing groups to practical NIPT are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic dissection of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to antisense oligonucleotides (nusinersen) that correct splicing and altered the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy. It is a clear case of RNA-processing biology becoming a transformative therapy and validating antisense medicine for genetic disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulation and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the decisive contributors named; earlier contributors on SMN gene identification (Melki, Lefebvre) and ISS-N1 target work (Singh) are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world and long-term data; independent confirmation by other approaches (risdiplam, gene therapy) supports the biology. Timely, with growing clinical evidence.
uncertainties: Attribution of the SMN gene discovery and target site identification is incomplete in the supplied names.
Broader generalizability of antisense approach beyond a few diseases is still developing.
